As used in this ordinance, the following terms shall have the respective meanings ascribed to them, unless the context otherwise requires:

Alcoholic beverage: All beer, malt beverages, wine and fortified wine as defined in this section. Distilled spirits are specifically excluded from the definition of this term, with regards to the interpretation of this ordinance and are not currently authorized for sale and distribution within the unincorporated areas of Treutlen County, Georgia.

Beer and malt beverage: Any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than twenty-one (21%) percent alcohol by volume, and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer and strong beer. The term “malt beverage” does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine. This definition includes hard cider.

Licensee: The individual to whom a license is issued or, in the case of partnership or corporation, all partners, officers and directors of the partnership or corporation.

Package: A bottle, can, keg, barrel or other original consumer container.

Premises: The definite closed or partitioned-in locality, whether room, shop, building, restaurant or club, wherein activities permitted by this ordinance are conducted.

Retailer or retail dealer: Any person who sells beer and/or wine, either in unbroken packages or for consumption on the premises, at retail only to consumers and not for resale.

Wine: Any alcoholic beverage containing not more than twenty-one (21%) percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries or grapes, either by fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. “Wine” includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, sake, and like products. The term “wine” does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at that point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this section. This definition may include those products marketed as “wine coolers”.
4: The sale and distribution of beer and wine is hereby authorized within the unincorporated area of Treutlen County, Georgia, subject to the provisions of state law authorizing counties to authorize the sale of the same; and subject to such regulations as have been or may be promulgated by the State of Georgia and to such regulations as have been or may be promulgated by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners.
5: A separate retail license shall be required for each place of business that seeks to sell beer and wine within Treutlen County. No single license may be shared or apply to separate and distinct locations.

11:
- (a) All persons, as owners, desiring to engage in activities permitted by this ordinance, shall make written application to the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners for the appropriate license, on forms prescribed by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners. All applications shall be accompanied by payment for the full amount of the license fee of seven hundred and fifty ($750.00) dollars and an investigative fee of one hundred and fifty ($150.00) dollars. If the application is denied, or if the applicant withdraws the application prior to its approval, the license fee ($750.00) shall be refunded, but the investigative fee ($150.00) shall be retained. Renewals of a license, once granted, will not require the payment of a new investigative fee, unless the license has previously been revoked or has lapsed.

- (b) The application shall include but shall not be limited to: The name and address of the applicant; the proposed business to be carried on; if a partnership, the names and residence addresses of the partners: if a corporation, the names and addresses of the officers, the name and address of the agent for service of process, the name and address of the manager, and the names and addresses of all shareholders holding more than ten (10%) percent of any class of corporate stock, or any other entity having a financial interest in each entity which is to own or operate the establishment. If the manager changes, the applicant must furnish the Treutlen County clerk with the name and address of the new manager and other information as requested within ten (10) days of such change. The applicant shall also disclose whether the applicant its partners if a partnership; its officers, manager, and shareholders having more than ten (10%) percent of any class of corporate stock if a corporation) has been convicted of any felony, misdemeanor or a violation of any municipal ordinance.

- (c) All applications shall be sworn to by the applicant before a notary public or other officer authorized to administer oaths, if applicable on the form.

- (d) The Treutlen County clerk or designee shall review the application and shall send a copy to the Treutlen County Sheriff, for investigation to determine compliance with Treutlen County regulations and laws and to investigate the criminal conviction history, in any, the character and reputation of the applicant. Following proper investigation, the Treutlen County Sheriff shall report his findings to the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners, for further consideration. If no report is received within thirty (30) days after forwarding to the Treutlen County Sheriff, it shall be concluded that there is no objection.

- (e) The Treutlen County clerk shall cause to be published in the legal organ of Treutlen County, Georgia, once a week during the two weeks immediately preceding the date of the meeting at which the application is scheduled for consideration by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners, a notice which shall include the name and address of the applicant, the location for which the license is sought, the type of license applied for, and the time and place the application will be considered by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners.

- (f) The Treutlen County clerk shall have authority to prescribe, prepare and amend forms for new or renewal applications. All applicants shall furnish data, information and records as required by the Treutlen County clerk and to ensure compliance with the provisions of this chapter. Failure to furnish such data shall automatically serve to dismiss the application with prejudice.

- (g) Any untrue or misleading information contained in, or material statement omitted from, an original, renewal or transfer application for a license shall be cause for the denial or revocation thereof.

- (h) In all instances in which an application is denied under the provisions of this chapter, the applicant may not reapply for a license for at least one (1) year from the final date of such denial.

- (i) Each applicant shall certify that applicant has read this ordinance, and if a license is granted, each licensee shall maintain a copy of this ordinance on the premises and shall require each of licensee’s employees to be familiar with this ordinance.
12:
- (a) No license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be granted to any person who is not a citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence.

- (b) No retailer or consumption on premises license will be granted to any person who is not a resident of the State of Georgia.

- (c) Corporations and partnerships. (1) If the applicant is a partnership or corporation, the provisions of this section shall apply to all its partners, officers, managers and majority stockholders. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the provisions of

subsections (a) and (b) of this section shall be waived for a corporation if the following shall be established:

- a. All majority stockholders of the corporation shall meet all the provisions of this section other than those provided in subsections (a) and (b);

- b. The corporation:

- 1. Is qualified and registered to do business within the state;

- 2. Has and continuously maintains in the following counties: Treutlen, Emanuel, Laurens, Johnson, Montgomery or Toombs, a registered agent who is a resident of the county, and upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this chapter to be served upon the licensee may be served; and

- 3. Consents to being subject to the jurisdiction and venue of the courts in this county.

The licensee shall file written proof of compliance with the foregoing, as well as its agent’s written consent to serve as agent and its consent to be subject to the jurisdiction and venue of the courts in this county with the Treutlen County clerk in such form as the Treutlen County clerk may prescribe; and

- (2) If the licensee shall be a corporation, the license shall be issued jointly to the corporation and to the majority stockholders, if such stockholders are individuals: Provided, however, that if stock in the corporation is traded on any of the national stock exchanges the license shall be issued jointly to the corporation and its agent registered under the provisions of this section. Where the majority stockholder is not an individual, then the license shall be issued jointly to the corporation and its agent registered under the provisions of this section. In the case of a partnership, the license will be issued to one of the partners.

- (d) No license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be granted to any person who, within twenty-four (24) months prior to the filing of the application for such license, has been convicted under any federal, state or local law, of any misdemeanor involving moral turpitude or of any felony or a violation of the guidelines set out by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners pertaining to

alcoholic beverages.

- (e) No license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be granted to any person who has had any beer and wine license revoked within two (2) years prior to the filing of the application.

- (f) The Treutlen County clerk may decline to issue a license when any person having any interest in the operation or control of such establishment does not meet the same character requirements as herein set forth for the licensee.

- (g) All licensed establishments must have and continuously maintain in the county a registered agent upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this chapter to be served upon the licensee may be served. This person must be a resident of the county. The licensee shall file the name of such agent, along with the written consent of such agent, with the Treutlen County clerk in such form as the clerk may prescribe.

- (h) In determining whether or not any license shall be granted, in addition to the other provisions of this chapter, the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners shall consider the following factors, in the public interest and welfare: (1) If applicant holds or has previously held a license to sell alcoholic beverages, and whether or not such applicant has violated any law, regulation or ordinance relating to such license or the business conducted pursuant to such license; (2) whether applicant has previously had a license to sell alcoholic beverages suspended or revoked; (3) Any negative investigation findings reported by the Treutlen County Sheriff; and (4) Any information obtained by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners from the public, as a result of its consideration of the application at a meeting of the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners.

- (a) Before a license shall be granted, the applicant shall comply with all Treutlen County rules and regulations pertaining to the sale of alcoholic beverages, and each applicant shall pay a license fee in accordance with the scale fixed, from time to time, by the council and kept on file in the office of the Treutlen County clerk.

- (b) All licenses shall be granted for the full calendar year or for the number of months remaining in the calendar year. Any applicant granted a license before July first (1s) shall pay the full license fee without proration. License fees for licenses granted on or after July first shall be prorated based on the number of months remaining in the calendar year; partial months shall be counted as a full

month.

14: All licenses granted hereunder shall expire on December thirty-first of each year. Licensees who desire to renew their license shall file a renewal application accompanied by the requisite license fee with the Treutlen County clerk upon forms prescribed by the Treutlen County clerk on or before November fifteenth (15) of each year without penalty, and not later than December fifteenth. Applications for renewal filed after November fifteenth and on or before December fifteenth shall be subject to a penalty of ten (10%) percent of the license fee. No renewal license shall be granted on applications filed after December fifteenth, but such applications shall be treated as an initial application and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules and regulations for the granting of licenses as if no previous license had been issued.

- (a) No license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be transferable, except as otherwise provided herein.

- (b) In case of the death of a licensee, the establishment shall be allowed to continue to sell alcoholic beverages for a period of forty-five (45) days from the date of death, or until expiration of the license, or until approval of a new licensee, whichever shall first occur; provided, that no sale of alcoholic beverages shall be allowed until such time as a personal representative of the estate, appointed by a probate court of competent jurisdiction, shall make application for authorization with the Treutlen County clerk.

- (c) In the event that a license is surrendered, or a licensee severs such person’s association with a licensed establishment, the establishment may continue to sell alcoholic beverages for a period of forty-five (45) days from the date of surrender, or from the date determined to be the date of severance; provided, that no such sale shall be authorized until such time as a new application for a license is made, such application indicating that no change of ownership has occurred, except as excepted herein. Upon issuance of a new license, the authorization to sell under the previous license shall be revoked by operation of law. No additional license fees shall be required during the period for which the original license was issued.

- (d) Nothing in this section, however, shall prohibit one or more of the partners in a partnership holding a license to withdraw from the partnership in favor of one or more of the partners who were partners at the time of the issuance of the license. This section shall not prohibit transfer of stock between persons who held stock in the corporate owner at the time of issuance of the license, nor shall it prohibit transfers of stock which do not result in any person increasing such person’s stock holdings to a total of ten (10%) percent or more of any class of stock.

- (e) Should a transfer of location be approved, with no change of ownership of the business, the license fee paid for the old location shall be applied to the new location.

- (f) Except as provided above, any change in the ownership of any entity owning a licensed establishment shall cancel and revoke any license issued hereunder automatically without the necessity of any hearing.

- (g) Violation of this section shall result in revocation of the license being used. and a fine as provided for in this ordinance. No license will be issued to the old or the new owner in the city for one year from the date of the violation.

- (a) All licensees must, within six (6) months after the approval of the license, open for business the establishment referred to in the application and license, and begin the sale of the products authorized by the license. Failure to open the establishment and begin the sale as referred to above within the six (6) month’s period shall serve as automatic forfeiture and cancellation of the license, and no refund of the license fee shall be made to the license holder.

- (b) Any licensee who shall for a period of three (3) consecutive months cease to operate the business and sale of the products authorized in the license, shall, after such three (3) month’s period automatically forfeit the license, which license shall be cancelled without the necessity of any further action, and without refund of the license fee to the license holder.

- (c) A license may be suspended or revoked by the Treutlen County clerk where the licensee furnishes fraudulent or untruthful information in the application for a license or omits information required in the application for a license and for failure to pay any fees, taxes or other charges imposed under the provisions of this chapter.

- (d) Whenever the State of Georgia, or any authorized officer or agency acting thereunder shall revoke any permit or license to sell alcoholic beverages, the Treutlen County license shall thereupon be automatically revoked. The Treutlen County Sheriff, upon notice of this revocation, shall take the necessary steps to see that signs are removed and that all alcoholic beverage sales cease.

- (i) An act or omission of a licensee, owner of more than ten (10%) percent interest in the licensed establishment, or employee of the licensee or licensed establishment willingly or knowingly performed, which constitutes a violation of federal or state law or of any provision of this chapter will subject the licensee to suspension or revocation of the license in accordance with the provisions of this chapter when the Treutlen County clerk determines to such clerk’s own satisfaction that the act or omission did occur, regardless of whether any criminal prosecution or conviction ensues; provided, however, in the case of an employee, the Treutlen County clerk must determine that the acts of the employee were known to or under reasonable circumstances should have been known to the licensee, were condoned by the licensee, or where the licensee has not established practices or procedures to prevent the violation from occurring.

- (a) The Treutlen County Board of Commissioners shall have the duty of hearing appeals from decisions of the Treutlen County clerk revoking or suspending a license.

- (b) No license shall be denied, suspended or revoked without the opportunity

11

for a hearing as hereinafter provided.

- (c) The Treutlen County clerk shall provide written notice to the applicant or licensee of such clerk’s order to deny, suspend or revoke the license. Such written notification shall set forth, in reasonable detail, the reasons for such action and shall notify the applicant or licensee of the right to appeal under the provisions of this chapter. Any applicant or licensee who is aggrieved or adversely affected by a final action of the Treutlen County clerk may have a review thereof by appeal to the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners. Such appeal shall be by written petition, filed in the office of the Treutlen County clerk within fifteen (15) days after the final order or action of the Treutlen County clerk. Any failure to file a timely written appeal shall be regarded as an affirmative waiver of all further due process.

- (d) A hearing shall be conducted on each appeal within thirty (30) days of the date of filing with the Treutlen County clerk, unless a continuance of such date is agreed to by the appellant and the Treutlen County clerk. The appellant at such hearing shall have the right to be represented by an attorney, at the expense of the appellant.

- (e) The findings of the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners shall be forwarded to the Treutlen County clerk after the conclusion of the hearing and it shall be the duty of the Treutlen County clerk to notify the appellant of the action of the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners.

- (f) The findings of the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners shall not be set aside unless found to be: (1) contrary to law or ordinance; or (2) unsupported by substantial evidence on the record as a whole; or (3) clearly unreasonable,

- (g) The findings of the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners shall be final unless appealed within thirty (30) days of the date of the findings to the superior court of the county.

- (h) For the purpose of this chapter, notice shall be deemed delivered when personally served or, when served by mail, within three (3) days after the date of deposit in the United States mail.

- (a) There is hereby levied and imposed upon the sale of beer and malt beverages within the unincorporated area of Treutlen County a specific excise tax as follows:

- (1) Where malt beverages and beer are sold in or from a barrel or bulk container, a tax of six ($6.00) dollars on each container sold containing not more than fifteen and one-half (15.5) gallons and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of fifteen and one-half (15.5) gallons;

- (2) Where beer and malt beverages are sold in bottles, cans, or other containers, except barrel or bulk containers, a tax of five cents ($0.05) per twelve (12) ounces and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional

16

parts of twelve (12) ounces.

- (b) The excise taxes provided for in this section shall be imposed upon and shall be paid by the licensed wholesale dealer in beer and malt beverages. Each wholesale dealer selling beer and malt beverages within Treutlen County shall file a report with Treutlen County by the tenth (10t) day of each month showing for the preceding calendar month the exact quantities of beer and malt beverages by size and type of container, sold during the month within Treutlen County. Each such wholesale dealer shall remit to Treutlen County on the tenth day of the month next succeeding the calendar month in which such sales were made, the amount of excise tax due in accordance with this section.

- (a) There is hereby levied and imposed upon the sale of wine within the unincorporated area of Treutlen County, a specific excise tax in the amount of twenty-two ($0.22) cents per liter and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of a liter.

- (b) The taxes imposed by this section shall not be levied with respect to:

Each such person shall remit to Treutlen on the tenth day of the month next succeeding the calendar month in which such sales were made, the amount of excise tax due in accordance with this section.
